probes.question: How was earth moved to build Cahokia's mounds?
True or false: around 1100 AD, Cahokia had a population of between 15,000 and 20,000 people.

image.alt: Monks Mound at Cahokia, a huge grass-covered earthen mound with a wooden staircase up its face under a wide blue sky
image.credit: User: (WT-shared) Ethajek at wts wikivoyage / Wikimedia Commons

body.claim: Around 1100 AD, Cahokia covered about 6 square miles (16 km²), included about 120 earthworks, and had a population of between 15,000 and 20,000 people.
body.why: Thousands of workers over decades moved more than an estimated 55 million cubic feet (1,600,000 m³) of earth in woven baskets to create this network of mounds and community plazas. Monks Mound, for example, rises 100 ft (30 m).
